results.note: persist_board (pipeline.py:566-602) is one generic loop over run.indicators keyed by registry entry, with no per-category branch beyond unwrapping the shared Ok-subtype pattern (FundingRateOk/OpenInterestOk/etc). Test asserts the function source contains no _active_addresses/_mvrv/_exchange_flow/_staking special-casing.
Drives heartbeat.main() end to end and asserts exactly 70 of 71 registered cells (every cell but sol_active_addresses) persist in one run with exactly one success ping.

Fixed from the prior rejected attempt: active_address_definitions (pipeline.py:390-395) is now filtered by excluded_keys BEFORE the fetch loop at pipeline.py:529-532, so run_scheduled_board() (pipeline.py:547-552, excluded_indicator_keys=(SOL_ACTIVE_ADDRESSES_KEY,)) never calls the active-addresses fetcher for SOL at all — not just discards its result. Test's fetch_scheduled_active_addresses (test_persist_board.py:1130-1134) asserts `asset != "SOL"` inside the monkeypatched fetcher, proving the slow fetch is never invoked on the scheduled path.

Forces an ETH MVRV fetch failure and asserts it persists as an Error row while btc_rsi (technical), btc_funding_rate (derivatives), btc_active_addresses and sol_staking (on-chain) all still persist successfully in the same run.

Pre-existing, still exercised tests: a board with one ERROR-status cell still pings success once persistence completes, while a raised exception during persist pings the /fail endpoint (test_heartbeat.py:80, test_failed_run_pings_the_failure_endpoint_rather_than_staying_silent).

Calls heartbeat.main() — the real module-level entry point matching `python -m ingest.heartbeat` in ingest.yml — which is wired through run_ingestion -> run_scheduled_board -> run_all_assets -> run_pipeline -> persist_board -> persist_datapoint; only network-touching fetchers/db/http are substituted, the production call chain itself is exercised.
Calls heartbeat.main_sol_active_addresses() end to end (the entry point invoked by sol-active-addresses.yml) and asserts it persists exactly one sol_active_addresses row for SOL and pings once.

ingest.yml declares timeout-minutes: 10 and runs `python -m ingest.heartbeat` (main() -> run_scheduled_board()). Unlike the rejected attempt, run_scheduled_board now genuinely excludes the SOL active-addresses fetch before it happens (see C3), so the actual scheduled job as configured no longer performs the ~2.5h fetch and fits its timeout.

New dedicated workflow: cron '43 3 * * 0' (weekly), timeout-minutes: 210 (comfortably above the ~2.5h fetch), runs `main_sol_active_addresses()` which fetches only sol_active_addresses — correctly isolated from the rest of the board.

note: Attempt 2 fixes the exact defect the prior verifier caught: active_address_definitions is now filtered by excluded_indicator_keys before the fetch loop runs (pipeline.py:390-395, 529-532), so run_scheduled_board() never invokes the slow SOL fetcher at all rather than discarding its result afterward.
